headline: Hiring a San Diego County Contractor for a Tub-to-Shower Conversion
articleBody:
Replacing a bathtub with a shower can improve access, update an aging bathroom, and make better use of limited floor area. The right scope depends on plumbing locations, wall and floor conditions, shower dimensions, ventilation, fixture choices, accessibility goals, and local permit requirements. A qualified remodeling team should evaluate these factors before preparing a firm proposal.

## What the Conversion Usually Includes

A typical project may involve removing the tub, inspecting the framing and subfloor, preparing the shower base, installing waterproof wall materials, connecting plumbing, fitting controls and a showerhead, and completing glass, trim, tile, or other finishes. Keeping the new shower near the existing tub location can reduce disruption, but concealed damage or requested layout changes can expand the work.

The proposal should distinguish demolition, plumbing, electrical, ventilation, waterproofing, finish materials, permit coordination, inspections, and cleanup. Ask whether the quoted scope includes removal and disposal of the old tub and what happens if concealed damage is found after demolition.

## What Can Change the Right Choice

A low-threshold or curbless shower may be attractive for easier entry, but the floor structure, drain location, waterproofing details, and finished elevations must be assessed before it is promised. A standard shower base may offer a more predictable installation when the existing floor cannot be recessed without additional work.

Think about who will use the bathroom. A handheld sprayer, strategically placed controls, a built-in or fold-down seat, grab-bar reinforcement, and slip-resistant flooring may be worthwhile even when full accessibility is not required. These decisions are easiest to address before walls are closed.

## Permits, Safety, and San Diego County Planning

Bathroom alterations can involve regulated plumbing, electrical, mechanical, or building work. San Diego County guidance states that required permits must be obtained before covered work begins, so the contractor and homeowner should confirm the applicable jurisdiction and permit scope before demolition. Local requirements can differ among San Diego, Chula Vista, Coronado, National City, Imperial Beach, and other communities.

Bathrooms with showers generally need mechanical ventilation for humidity control, and electrical work near water requires appropriate protection and placement. The project should also account for current water-conserving fixture requirements when applicable, particularly in older homes undergoing improvements.

## Questions to Ask Before Hiring

- Will the team inspect the subfloor, framing, drain, supply lines, and existing waterproofing before finalizing the scope?
- Is the shower base custom, prefabricated, or site-built, and who is responsible for waterproofing details?
- Which permits and inspections are included, and who schedules them?
- What products and installation methods will be used at corners, niches, benches, and pipe penetrations?
- How will change orders be documented if hidden damage is discovered?
- Does the design account for ventilation, lighting, storage, and future support bars?

Elite Remodeling & Design, Inc. describes a coordinated design-build process that can extend from consultation and design development through permitting, construction, and final inspection. Homeowners can use that process to discuss layout, 3D design visualization, material selections, and plumbing or electrical coordination before work starts.

## Key Takeaways

- Keep the new shower near existing plumbing when practical, but verify conditions first.
- Decide early whether access features or a curbless design are priorities.
- Confirm permit and inspection responsibilities for the specific local jurisdiction.
- Require waterproofing, concealed-condition allowances, and exclusions in writing.
